Mass of an Atom at One Point, by Observation

Source: R/truncated.R
atom_mass_at.Rd

Returns the probability that a distribution with atoms places on the single point x, one value per observation. distrib_atoms() reports the masses at the first observation's parameters, so a parameter that varies by observation is read one row at a time.

Usage

atom_mass_at(parent, x, theta)

Arguments

parent

A distribution object that may declare atoms.

x

A single number, the point.

theta

A named list of the parent's parameters. A component may vary by observation.

Value

A numeric vector with one mass per observation (a single number for scalar parameters), zero where x is not an atom.

See also

parent_mass_at(), which calls it for a continuous parent, and expectation.TruncatedContinuousDistrib().

Examples

za <- zero_adjusted(gamma2_distrib())
distributions7:::atom_mass_at(za, 0, list(mu = c(1, 4), sigma2 = 1,
                                          za = c(0.3, 0.6)))
#> [1] 0.3 0.6
